name: hmac_sha256_body
use_for: Generic body-only HMAC with a hex signature (GitHub's `sha256=<hex>`, custom partners). Shopify signs in base64: use the string form `verify: shopify`.
optional: prefix (e.g. 'sha256='; when declared the header must start with it)
yaml:
on:
  request:
    method: POST
    path: /api/webhooks/github
    verify:
      recipe: hmac_sha256_body
      header: X-Hub-Signature-256
      prefix: "sha256="
      secret: "{{ env.GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET }}"
note: expected = hex(hmac_sha256(secret, body)). Caller's signature is compared after prefix stripping, in constant time. A declared prefix is required: a header without it fails (401) and is not compared as bare hex.

name: hmac_timestamp_dot_body
use_for: Senders that sign `<timestamp>.<body>` and send the timestamp in its own header. Includes replay-window protection. Not Slack (it signs `v0:<ts>:<body>`: use `verify: slack`), not Stripe (`verify: stripe`), not a Benmore subscription (`verify: benmore`).
optional: prefix (required in the header when declared)
yaml:
on:
  request:
    method: POST
    path: /api/webhooks/notifier
    verify:
      recipe: hmac_timestamp_dot_body
      header: X-Notifier-Signature
      timestamp_header: X-Notifier-Timestamp
      secret: "{{ env.NOTIFIER_SECRET }}"
      skew_seconds: 300
note: expected = hex(hmac_sha256(secret, ts + "." + body)). Stale timestamps (outside skew_seconds) are rejected even when the signature itself is valid - that's the replay-attack guard. skew_seconds 0 (or omitted) means 300. A negative skew_seconds disables the check only when the app's env sets WEBHOOK_SKEW_ALLOW_NEGATIVE=1 (meant for tests); without it a negative value is treated as 0, so the 300-second window stays on. skew_seconds above 86400 (one day) is refused at write time, and a saved flow with a larger value is held to 86400 at runtime; a declared prefix must start the signature header.

name: hmac_sha1_body
use_for: Raw-body HMAC-SHA1 providers such as Autodesk Platform Services webhooks, with bounded current/previous-secret rotation.
yaml:
on:
  request:
    method: POST
    path: /api/webhooks/autodesk
    auth: none
    verify:
      recipe: hmac_sha1_body
      header: X-Adsk-Signature
      prefix: "sha1hash="
      secret: "${{ env.AUTODESK_WEBHOOK_SECRET }}"
      previous_secret: "${{ env.AUTODESK_WEBHOOK_SECRET_PREVIOUS }}"
note: expected = hex(hmac_sha1(secret, exact raw body)). The current and optional previous secret are both checked in constant time. Omit previous_secret after the provider's rotation overlap ends; if configured, it must resolve to a non-empty env value.

name: hmac_sha256_path_bearer
use_for: Per-subscription webhook bearer credentials derived from an opaque URL handle without storing one secret per subscription (for example Procore destination_headers).
yaml:
on:
  request:
    method: POST
    path: /api/webhooks/procore/:handle
    auth: none
    verify:
      recipe: hmac_sha256_path_bearer
      secret: "${{ env.PROCORE_WEBHOOK_MASTER_SECRET }}"
      prefix: "Bearer "
      path_param: handle
      context: "procore-webhook:"
note: Authorization must equal prefix + hex(hmac_sha256(master secret, context + path value)). path_param must name a dynamic segment in this route and match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*. The opaque handle is routing data, not a credential; never put the derived bearer in a URL, response, or database.
